The homepage remains unmistakably product-first: “Product leadership for public-facing systems,” a discovery-to-handoff lifecycle, three public-product cases, and a senior-role call to action establish Jamie’s professional position before the practice lineage is introduced.

Two-click legibility passes. About is one primary-navigation click from the homepage on desktop and mobile; its through-line directly links HJE, WOWList, Sunday Dinner/196, Fair Rent/NYC Artist Coalition, and Source-Backed Team Memory as second-click evidence.

About explicitly names the practice as “artistic, civic, technical, and social” and explains why these are inhabited systems: people must recognize relationships, participate, remember what happened, influence the work, and continue it.

Continuity one—Sunday Dinner/196: hospitality, trust, shared place, artist support, recurring participation, and care become invitation, hosting, onboarding, access-handoff, minimal-documentation, and follow-through systems. Two redacted workflow reconstructions make continuity inspectable while preserving artist agency and participant privacy.

Continuity two—NYC Artist Coalition/FairRentNYC: attention to lived cultural-space experience, meetings, public sources, questions, and accountable actors becomes testimony, campaign interfaces, town halls, source maps, decision records, minutes, and action trackers that collaborators can inhabit and carry forward.

Continuity three—HJE: attention to customer language, institutional voice, product judgment, and team habits becomes an integrated commerce-and-operations system refined through use, then preserved through reusable patterns, ownership, documentation, and next actions.

WOWList reinforces the artistic-technical-social continuity: organizers’ existing language for scenes, interests, venues, and places becomes followable keyword communities, distributed publishing, digests, calendars, support practices, and reusable deployment patterns.

Open House supplies bounded artistic lineage through a public article and governed claim: Jamie initiated the ten-day experiment, while communal decision-making and many-perspective documentation remain participant-governed rather than converted into solo authorship.

Collective credit is visible and specific: WOWList is co-built and credits collaborators; FairRentNYC distinguishes Jamie’s implementation and organizing from collective advocacy, report authorship, legislative enactment, or sole causation; Sunday Dinner credits its community; HJE credits the company team.

The scoped desktop renders preserve the hierarchy and boundaries: the homepage is product-led, About makes the interdisciplinary through-line readable, and the project pages expose sources, Known/Open/Protected states, care limits, and credits. The render audit reports no horizontal overflow, broken images, or console errors for the corresponding desktop and mobile routes.
